title: Post-thrombotic syndrome after a leg clot
intro: Post-thrombotic syndrome is a long-term complication of deep vein thrombosis, a blood clot in the leg veins. The clot can damage vein valves and cause lasting pain, swelling and skin changes in the affected leg. Not everyone develops it, and treatment focuses on easing symptoms and preventing further problems.

sections.heading: How it develops
paragraphs: After a clot in a deep vein, the vein wall and its valves may be damaged by the clot or scarring. Damaged valves fail to keep blood moving upward, so blood pools in the leg and pressure rises. Symptoms may appear months to years after the thrombosis. A clot above the knee, repeated clots and being overweight raise the risk.

sections.heading: Symptoms
paragraphs: Typical symptoms are a heavy, aching or tired leg, swelling that worsens through the day, cramps, itching or tingling, enlarged surface veins, darkening and hardening of the skin around the ankle and in severe cases open sores called venous ulcers. Symptoms often worsen with standing and ease with leg elevation.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
paragraphs: Doctors diagnose based on symptoms, a history of thrombosis and examination, supported by ultrasound to assess the veins and exclude new clots. Scoring systems grade severity. Sudden swelling, pain and redness may be a new clot and need urgent assessment.

sections.heading: Treatment and self-care
paragraphs: Compression stockings can reduce swelling and discomfort in many people when worn consistently, though evidence of benefit is mixed. Regular walking, calf exercises, elevating the legs during rest, avoiding long standing or sitting and weight loss help. Skin care with moisturisers prevents cracking. Medicines to improve circulation have limited proof. Ulcers need specialised wound care, with compression therapy as the foundation. Procedures or surgery on veins are rarely used.

sections.heading: Prevention
paragraphs: Take prescribed anticoagulants for the recommended period after a clot, stay active, keep a healthy weight, and use compression and movement during long journeys when advised. After surgery or illness, follow guidance to prevent clots. Early treatment of thrombosis reduces the risk of damage.

examples.title: Managing swelling
examples.text: Imagine your leg swells by the evening. You could wear compression stockings in the morning, walk regularly and raise your leg above heart level for a time in the evening.

examples.title: Protecting skin
examples.text: Suppose the skin near your ankle is dry and dark. You might moisturise daily and see your doctor promptly if a wound or redness develops.
